It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth” through digital streams that capture the gaze of the young, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the formation of loves and the discipling of our children’s attention in this hour? [1, 1330, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” in the form of algorithms that “do not spare the flock,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the hearts of the next generation? [13, 20, 1143, 1425, 1532, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “common ground” with a culture that “cater[s] to people’s itching ears,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” [11, 28, 1336, 1503, 1515, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the competition for a child's heart is not an “administrative anomaly” but a “savage spiritual conflict” where the “spotless purity of truth must always be at war with the blackness of heresy and lies” [15, 68, 1143, 1328, 1366, 1532, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Deformation of Desires (The Heart as a Factory of Idols)**

**Verse**
“Because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God, nor were thankful, but became futile in their thoughts, and their foolish hearts were darkened. Professing to be wise, they became fools” (Romans 1:21–22). [1087, 1362, 1594, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that “unbelief is the seed” of all disordered love, for “the carnal mind is enmity against God” (Romans 8:7) [1338, 1500, 1643, Conversation History]. Our desires are “deformed” when we “exchange the truth about God for a lie and worship and serve the creature rather than the Creator,” turning the heart into a “thoroughfare” for “the mixed multitude of iniquities” (Romans 1:25) [205, 1405, 1595, Conversation History]. Reformed theology—echoed by **John MacArthur**—notes that “men loved darkness rather than light” because “sin is the monarch that rules the heart of every man,” leading us to “love the world” and its “lust of the eyes” (John 3:19; 1 John 2:15) [11, 72, 73, 765, 798, 1365, 1406, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “worldly philosophy” that says all desires are “natural and good,” for “your life is not your own” because you were “bought at a price” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20) [12, 91, 101, 257, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must instead “tremble at My word” (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2) [251, 851, 1039, 1381, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” were “punctilious” about “legal minutiae,” yet their hearts were “stiff-necked” because they “rejected the word of the LORD” (Matthew 23:23; 1 Samuel 15:23) [8, 176, 204, 1091, 1333, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our standing by showing that “true circumcision is that of the heart,” and we find “repose of the soul” not in “ritualized ceremonies” but in “the washing of regeneration” (Romans 2:29; Titus 3:5) [13, 24, 142, 358, 802, 1214, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Discipling Attention in the Digital Age**

**Verse**
“And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God” (Romans 12:2). [146, 808, 868, 1550, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition asserts that “we are the products of our thinking,” and therefore, a mind that is constantly fed by “media empires” and “electronic age” stories will be “tossed to and fro... by the trickery of men” (Ephesians 4:14; Proverbs 23:7) [142, 296, 458, 1459, 1462, 1506, Conversation History]. Algorithms operate by “catering to people’s itching ears,” offering “spiritual placebos” that “muffle the truth of God’s Word” with “trivial diversions” (2 Timothy 4:3) [37, 213, 1336, 1483, Conversation History]. The “spirit of fraud” in modern technology seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth,” yet “God has spoken with the utmost clarity” through the “propositions of Scripture” [11, 1325, 1330, 1378, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Saturate and renew your mind” with the “more sure Word,” recognizing that “the heart of the wise teaches his mouth” to resist the “futility of their mind” (Psalm 119:105; Proverbs 16:23; Ephesians 4:17) [11, 21, 101, 105, 116, 562, 907, 1210, 1313, 1406, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” refusing to let the “god of this age” blind your eyes with “cleverly devised myths” (1 Corinthians 9:27; 2 Corinthians 4:4; 2 Peter 1:16) [13, 20, 79, 116, 143, 1228, 1313, 1342, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Moralism vs. Regeneration**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” was a “temporal sign” of favor, yet many Jews used the law to “establish their own righteousness” (Romans 10:3) [316, 409, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” teaching that “victory that has overcome the world” is “our faith” in the “finished work” of Christ, not in a “patchwork religion” of “human ingenuity” (1 John 5:4; John 19:30) [24, 136, 1066, 1313, 1445, 1506, 1580, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Mandate of Parents and Shepherds**

**Verse**
“And these words which I command you today shall be in your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up” (Deuteronomy 6:6–7). [832, 1277, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—notes that “parents [are] instructed [to teach] the children within the home,” creating a “spiritual legacy” that resists “the iniquity of the fathers” (Deuteronomy 6:7) [1277, 1343, 1600, Conversation History]. We are commanded to “bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord,” for “training up a child in the way he should go” ensures they will “not depart from it” (Ephesians 6:4; Proverbs 22:6) [1136, 1166, Conversation History]. Discipleship is the “Great Commission” of the home, where we “warn those who are unruly” and “equip the saints” to “test all things” (Matthew 28:19–20; 1 Thessalonians 5:21) [90, 169, 294, 1007, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for your “daily bread” is provided by a “loving, beneficent Father” who “will not let your foot slip” (Matthew 6:11; Psalm 121:3) [3, 28, 51, 94, 201, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. Your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” by “setting a pattern of good works” that our children may “glory in this, that he understands and knows Me” (Titus 2:7, 10; Jeremiah 9:24) [12, 33, 101, 361, 779, 1131, 1227, 1406, 1450, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Theocracy vs. Pilgrimage**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, “ national prosperity” was linked to “dwelling in your land safely,” but God still “removed kings” who “rejected the word of the LORD” (Leviticus 26:5; 1 Samuel 15:23) [15, 17, 409, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “citizenship,” showing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” looking for a “city whose builder and maker is God” (1 Peter 2:11; Hebrews 11:10) [13, 26, 38, 142, 440, 1236, 1251, 1313, 1320, 1426, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Hope of Redeemed Attention**

**Verse**
“And Him God has exalted to His right hand to be Prince and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins” (Acts 5:31). [914, 1247, 1249, 1300, 1431, Conversation History]. “Every branch in Me that does not bear fruit He takes away; and every branch that bears fruit He prunes, that it may bear more fruit” (John 15:2). [219, 934, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of a distracting world by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 23, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. On that Day, the “redeemed of the LORD” will be “faultless” before His glory, for “He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6; Jude 24) [5, 614, 796, 829, 940, 1132, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. Every “human monument” and “building enterprise” of the digital age will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away,” but the “unified church” will “dwell there throughout all of eternity” (Psalm 102:3) [11, 32, 35, 43, 66, 789, 806, 940, 1315, 1460, 1684, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Lord knows those who are His” and his “everlasting dominion” is “secure” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Timothy 2:19; Daniel 7:14) [11, 14, 24, 47, 92, 94, 109, 121, 147, 176, 201, 313, 412, 1132, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. Find “tranquility of soul” by “resting upon the surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “unsearchable wisdom” will preserve our children (Psalm 138:2; Ephesians 3:10) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 352, 412, 1012, 1132, 1143, 1306, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 311, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

Prayer is fitting at any time, in any posture, in any place, under any circumstance, and in any attire. It is to be a total way of life—an open and continual communion with God. After having embraced all the infinite resources that are yours in Christ, don’t ever think you’re no longer dependent on the moment-by-moment power of God.

For Paul, and for any mature Christian, prayer is a permanent state of mind by which the promises and purposes of God, the spiritual well-being of His people, the advance of His gospel, and the growth of His church are passionately desired. What concerns the Lord must concern you if you truly desire to glorify Him in your life. The Requests Paul’s prayer for the Thessalonians contains three vital and dynamic spiritual issues that are critical for all believers: “That our God will count you worthy of your calling, and fulfill every desire for goodness and the work of faith with power” (2 Thess. 1:11). Worthiness refers to spiritual character. It should be our desire that the Lord would make us the kind of people we ought to be. Fulfillment speaks of God bringing about in our lives every holy longing. And power is necessary for our service to be truly effective. When you pray for your loved ones or for fellow brothers and sisters in Christ, pray for their worthiness, fulfillment, and power in service. When those issues are the priorities of our prayers and our patterns of obedience, God will be honored.

The Worldly Hearer The third type of soil, the weedy soil, represents a heart too enthralled or too preoccupied with worldly matters. Jesus explains, “Now the ones that fell among thorns are those who, when they have heard, go out and are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity” (Luke 8:14). Those who fit this category (like the shallow-soil hearers) may seem to respond positively at first. The analogy suggests that there will most likely be some initial sign of receptivity. Seed sown among weeds would germinate. These people, “when they have heard, go out”—meaning, apparently, that they give every sign of pursuing the way of faith. Mark seems to suggest that at first they seem to have every potential to be fruitful, but then at some point afterward, “the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful” (Mark 4:19, emphasis added).

Only God Himself can plow and prepare a heart to receive the Word. He does it through the regenerating and sanctifying work of His Holy Spirit, who convicts the world “of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment” (John 16:8). For those who believe, he awakens them spiritually (Rom. 8:11). He enlightens their minds to the truth (1 Cor. 2:10). He washes them clean (Ezek. 36:25). He removes the stony heart and gives them a new heart (v. 26). He indwells His people and motivates them unto righteousness (v. 27). He engraves the truth of God on their hearts (Jer. 31:33; 2 Cor. 3:3). He pours the love of God into their hearts (Rom. 5:5). We who believe in Christ are totally dependent on the indwelling Spirit’s work in our hearts to keep us tender, receptive, and ultimately fruitful.

five The Lord and Master (Part 2) The heroes of church history defended Christ’s headship, not on the basis of an arbitrary opinion or out of personal ambition, but because they found that truth unmistakably revealed in the Scriptures. Ephesians 5:23 states that “Christ . . . is the head of the church,” and Colossians 1:18 echoes, “He is also head of the body, the church; and He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that He Himself will come to have first place in everything.” In the first chapter of Ephesians, Paul explained that God the Father “put all things in subjection under His [Christ’s] feet, and gave Him as head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all” (vv. 22–23). Other New Testament Scriptures speak of growing “up in all aspects into Him who is the head” (Eph. 4:15) and “holding fast to the head, from whom the entire body . . . grows with a growth which is from God” (Col. 2:19).
